To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expression of PPR and CA IX in the examined panel of human breast and ovarian cell lines is not directly correlated with the amount of their mitochondria and that the PBR expression is related to the malignant progression in breast and resistance to chemotherapy in ovarian carcinoma.
PBR and CA IX are expressed in human breast and ovary carcinoma cell lines in a different way.

PBR expression correlates with the invasive potential of breast carcinoma cell lines and with resistance of ovarian carcinoma cell lines to cisplatin, and that CA IX expression in ovarian carcinoma cell lines correlates with resistance to adriamycin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new prognostically important parameters in breast and ovarian carcinomas.
the expression of new prognostically relevant markers in breast and ovarian cancer cell lines and their potential application for clinical studies.
the identification and quantitation of new markers in breast and ovarian cancer cell lines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PBR is a prognostic factor in breast carcinoma and CA IX is a marker of hypoxically induced resistance in ovarian carcinoma.
PBR and CA IX expression in breast and ovary carcinoma cell lines is a function of the cell line origin and the cell density.
PBR and CA IX may be useful markers of malignant progression in breast and ovarian cancer, but the prognostic value of these markers needs further validation in a large clinical study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of PGR and CA IX in breast and ovarian cell lines is related to the malignant potential of these cells.
PBR and CA IX could serve as prognostic markers in the panel of breast and ovarian carcinoma lines and that PBR could be used as a target for therapy of invasive and resistant tumors.
both PBR and CA IX are promising new prognostic and predictive markers in breast and ovarian carcinomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of both antigents in breast and ovarian cell lines can be considered as prognostic markers.
the expression of PPR in breast and ovarian cancer cell lines should be expressed relatively, not absolutely, to mitochondrial mass.
both antigens are promising markers for prognosis and prediction of response to therapy.
